title: raw rpyc _check_existing_position skips initialize() — returns None when MT5 terminal shutdown
problem: Both swing trader (live_trader.py:803) and m5_scalp trader (m5_scalp_trader.py:523) use raw rpyc.connect() + conn.root.positions_get() WITHOUT calling conn.root.initialize() first. MT5Bridge wrapper used by live_collector calls initialize() then shutdown() each cycle (fetch_candles_sync), so the MT5 terminal in Wine flips between initialized and shutdown states. When traders check positions while terminal is shutdown, positions_get returns None (not []). The traders treat None as 'bridge disconnected' and hold off new trades — but actually the bridge is fine, just not initialized. Race condition: timing decides whether trades happen. Verified hypothesis: calling initialize() before positions_get returns real account_info + list of positions.
solution: Added conn.root.initialize() call before conn.root.positions_get() in both raw rpyc code paths (live_trader.py:_check_existing_position line 803, m5_scalp_trader.py:_check_existing_m5_scalp_position line 523). Try/finally ensures shutdown() is called to leave terminal in clean state for next caller. If initialize() fails, falls back to existing 'bridge down' behavior. Causal tests in tests/test_check_position_initialize.py prove initialize() is called before positions_get() (RED→GREEN). Direct verification on Real-A: 5/5 rpyc calls from oracle-engine to mt5a succeeded with initialize=True, positions returned as list (not None). Regression: 709 tests passed.
notes: Found 2026-07-07 during post-deploy verification. Bug affects both swing and m5_scalp. Fix: use MT5Bridge wrapper or add explicit initialize() call before positions_get in raw rpyc paths.

title: Reconcile picks wrong deal — missing time filter (ISSUE-080)
problem: _match_closing_deal (db.py) and _reconcile_external_close (live_trader.py) Strategy 1 (price proximity) does NOT filter deals by time. When two trades cluster in a price neighborhood, an earlier trade's SL/TP close (which happened BEFORE this trade opened) can be the closest in price to this trade's entry, so Strategy 1 picks it. Bridge does not expose position_id/entry fields so Strategy 0 (position_id match) is unusable. Result: DB records wrong exit_price/pnl/exit_reason. On Real-A 2026-07-08: trade #5543 BUY @ 4124.679 — DB recorded exit=4132.34 pnl=+$7.66 (profit!) but MT5 actually closed at 4112.76 pnl=-$11.92 (loss). 3 of 9 Real-A trades had wrong exit data.

Strategy 1 now filters closing deals by deal.time > open_deal_time, excluding earlier-trade closes. 3 causal tests RED→GREEN. Fix applied to both _match_closing_deal (db.py) and _reconcile_external_close (live_trader.py). docker-compose: separate ML_FILTER_ENABLED_A env var for oracle-engine.
notes: CPT: tests/test_reconcile_time_filter.py. Learning: ψ/memory/learnings/2026-07-08_reconcile-time-filter.md. Fix: open_deal_time lookup (deal.order==ticket AND type==opening_type) + filter deal.time > open_deal_time in Strategy 1.

title: MT5 auto-login gives up permanently — no retry once terminal finishes booting

title: COPY . . bakes data/ 1.6GB into every image layer — disk exhaustion risk
problem: Dockerfile uses 'COPY . .' without .dockerignore, so data/ (oracle.db 1.4GB + farm DBs + paper feed) is baked into every build layer. On 2026-10-02 the disk hit 100% (117MB free) and builds failed mid-deploy; docker builder prune -af + buildx prune -af freed ~20GB (9.17 + 10.64GB), but the root cause remains: every future rebuild re-accumulates multi-GB layers until disk exhaustion recurs. Fix = repo-wide .dockerignore excluding data/ (and other runtime-only dirs). NOTE: needs approval before acting — the VPS image's runtime relies on some baked content, so the ignore list must be checked against what docker-compose.vps.yml containers actually read from the baked copy (esp. data/xau-data fallback).
solution: .dockerignore ทั้ง repo (data/ .git/ ψ/ tests/ graphify-out/ .env* *.db *.pkl *.joblib models) — oracle image 3.98GB→1.67GB (-2.3GB), ปิด class bake .env ที่มี MT5 credentials จริงทุก build (ISSUE-099 ตายถาวร); ปิด gap load_dotenv-no-op: docker-compose.yml pin RANGING_HARD_BLOCK + LEARNING_MODE — vps/farm compose ตรวจแล้ว pin ครบ ไม่ต้องแตะ (causal test: tests/test_dockerignore_contract_causal.py)

title: Watchdog alerts on its own tooling failures, not just farm problems
problem: scripts/farm_watchdog.py treats 'docker ps failed' / 'docker logs failed' as a farm problem and writes it to ψ/outbox/farm_alert_<date>.md. On its first real launchd fire (2026-10-02) the agent's minimal PATH had no docker, so the watchdog wrote a FALSE farm alert about docker being missing — the alert channel then contained a self-diagnostic, not a farm problem, which trains readers to distrust alert files. _docker_bin() fixed that specific instance, but the design flaw remains: any future tooling failure (docker daemon down, permissions) becomes a 'farm alert'. The watchdog should either separate self-errors (log-only, distinct message) from farm problems (alert file), or tag self-errors explicitly in the alert text so Hermes/หมอ can tell them apart.
notes: Found in retro 2026-10-02 22.45 (false farm_alert_2026-10-02.md was deleted manually after the PATH fix)
